encounters.title: Alien Contact
encounters.description: The signal arrives on no known frequency. Dave's communications officer frowns at the display. "Sir, this... isn't from any registered faction." Dave leans forward. The message resolves into a visual: vast, luminous beings drifting in the void between stars. Their voice arrives not through speakers but through the hull itself, a vibration felt in the bones. "Commander Dave of the Canis League. We have observed your campaign with interest. We offer an alternative to your current... trajectory."

outcome.description: The aliens describe a crystal resonance technology that could amplify or neutralize whisper crystal deposits at will. In League hands, it would end the resource war overnight. Dave listens without expression. Power of this magnitude always comes with strings attached.

choices.text: "The League deals in evidence, not promises. Prove your capability."

outcome.description: A nearby asteroid flickers, then erupts with crystal growth in seconds. Dave watches a dead rock become a fortune. His jaw tightens. This is real. This changes everything. "Noted," he says, because that is all he trusts himself to say.

choices.text: "Unknown entities offering power. That is the oldest trap in the book. Terminate the signal."

outcome.description: The aliens withdraw without protest. Dave stares at the empty void where they hovered. His instincts say he just refused the most dangerous gift in the multiverse. His duty says he was right to.

encounters.title: Aristotle Parley
encounters.description: Aristotle's ship appears at the edge of scanner range, broadcasting a parley flag. Dave studies the display. The cat is alone. No fleet. No ambush formation.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave watches the lone Corsair vessel drift closer on the tactical display. His first officer shifts uncomfortably. "It could be a trap, sir." Dave says nothing. He already knows it isn't.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Open the channel." Dave straightens his collar. "Captain Aristotle. You have five minutes."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Aristotle appears on screen. The grin is there, of course. It is always there. But something is different. The eyes don't match the mouth. "Dave, old boy. Miss me?"

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "You came alone. No escort. No fleet hiding in the debris field." Dave's eyes narrow. "Either this is the bravest move you have ever made, or the most desperate."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Can't it be both?" The grin wavers. Aristotle shifts in his captain's chair. "Look, Dave. I'm not here to trade insults. Something is coming. Something bigger than our little spat over fuel rights."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave catalogues every micro-expression. The twitch of Aristotle's whiskers. The way his claws grip the armrest. The cat is scared. That is new. That is very useful information. "Continue."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "The Sovereigns. Lions and Wolves both. They've been playing us against each other, Dave. While we've been bashing heads, they've been positioning fleets. I've seen the deployments. It's not posturing. It's an invasion corridor."

choices.text: "Show me the intelligence. If your data is solid, we can talk."

outcome.description: Aristotle transmits Corsair surveillance data. Dave's analysts confirm the Sovereign fleet movements. The cat is telling the truth. Dave does not respond immediately. He files the information and says, "Continue."

choices.text: "If you want to talk, surrender your crystal reserves first. Then we negotiate."

outcome.description: Aristotle's grin freezes. He transmits a partial crystal manifest. Not surrender. A gesture. Dave files it and says nothing. Gestures can be built upon.

choices.text: "Your five minutes are up. The next time we meet, it will be in combat."

outcome.description: Dave closes the channel. Aristotle's ship hangs in the void, then burns hard for Corsair space. Dave watches it go. Duty does not negotiate with pirates.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: Aristotle transmits the files. Star charts. Fleet dispositions. Intercepted communications. It is comprehensive. It is also an enormous risk—this data reveals Corsair intelligence capabilities.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave reviews the data in silence. His analysts confirm: the Sovereign movements are real. The invasion corridor is real. The timeline is weeks, not months.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Your intelligence is solid." A pause. "You are also terrified. I have never seen that on you before, Aristotle."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Yeah, well. Enjoy it while it lasts." The grin flickers back, but it's thin. "So. Do we keep killing each other for the Sovereigns' entertainment, or do we do something stupid and unprecedented?"

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "I will take this under advisement." Dave's expression betrays nothing. But he does not close the channel. That is, for Dave, practically an embrace.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: The grin freezes. "Surrender? That's your opening move? You really are a dog." But Aristotle doesn't cut the channel. After a long moment, he transmits a partial manifest. Twelve crystal caches. A fraction of his reserves.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave reviews the manifest. It is a gesture, not a surrender. But it is a gesture that costs Aristotle real resources. That means something.

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Received." Dave files the data without comment. "You may continue your briefing, Captain."

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Such warmth. Such hospitality." But the cat's shoulders relax a fraction. He has bought time. Dave has gained leverage. Both of them know it. Neither says it.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: The grin dies. For one unguarded moment, Aristotle looks exactly like what he is: a cat who has gambled everything and lost.

dialogue_steps.speaker: aristotle
dialogue_steps.text: "Still a dog on a leash, I see. When the Sovereigns eat you alive, remember I tried."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave closes the channel. He watches Aristotle's ship hang in the void for a long moment, then burn hard for Corsair space. His first officer asks, "Orders, sir?" Dave says, "Resume patrol." Duty does not negotiate with pirates. Even frightened ones.

encounters.title: Death's Offer
encounters.description: The ghost ship appears without warning. No warp signature, no sensor trace. Death's vessel fills the viewport like a splinter of absolute darkness.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: The comms activate on their own. Every screen on the bridge flickers to static, then resolves into shadow. Two burning eyes appear in the darkness. A purr rolls across the bridge like distant thunder.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Commander Dave. I have watched you hunt my kin with admirable patience. Such... discipline. Such restraint." The purr deepens. "It must be exhausting, being so controlled all the time."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Identify yourself. You are broadcasting on a League military frequency." Dave's voice is level. His hand rests near the alarm console. His crew does not move.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "You know who I am, Commander. Every shadow your patrols have chased. Every ship that vanished without a trace. I am the question mark in your reports." A pause. "I can deliver Aristotle to you. Bound. Broken. All I require is... a favour."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: Dave's expression does not change. But his crew notices his jaw tighten, the way it does before a difficult decision. "I am listening. But I will not commit to terms proposed by a ghost."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "When the dust settles, I want the Forgotten Realm. All of it. No League patrols. No jurisdiction. A kingdom of shadows where I answer to no one." The eyes flare brighter. "A small price for the pirate king's head, wouldn't you say?"

choices.text: "State the operational details. If they serve the League's interests, we have a provisional arrangement."

outcome.description: Death's purr deepens. A lawless zone in exchange for ending the Corsair threat. The math is ugly, but it works. "Provisionally accepted," Dave says.

choices.text: "The League does not make deals with shadows. Leave my bridge."

outcome.description: Death's eyes dim. "Pity. You are more principled than I expected. That will make this harder for everyone." The ghost ship fades. Principle means fighting alone.

choices.text: "I do not need you to deliver Aristotle. But I could use intelligence on his defences."

outcome.description: A low chuckle. "Shrewd. You want the fruit without the poison." Death transmits Corsair fleet positions, crystal caches, Aristotle's contingency plans. "Consider this a free sample."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Provisionally accepted. The Forgotten Realm becomes a demilitarized zone under your... administration. In exchange, I expect Aristotle's fleet neutralized within thirty standard days."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Thirty days." The purr becomes a rattling laugh. "You negotiated a deadline with Death. I admire the audacity, Commander."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Audacity has nothing to do with it. I operate on schedules." Dave's crew exchange uneasy glances. Their commander just made a deal with the void. Dave does not notice their discomfort. Or if he does, he files it under acceptable costs.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "Schedules. How very... canine." The shadow recedes. The bridge lights flicker back to full. Death's vessel vanishes as silently as it appeared. Dave stares at the empty void for exactly three seconds. Then turns to his officers. "Resume course."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: The eyes dim to sullen embers. "Pity. You are more principled than I expected, Commander. That will make this harder. For everyone."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "I have been making things hard for everyone my entire career. Leave."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: "As you wish." The shadows bleed away like smoke in a breeze. The bridge lights stabilize. Dave's officers release held breath. Dave does not. He will not exhale until the sensor sweep confirms the ghost ship is truly gone. Principle is expensive. He can afford it.

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: A pause. Then a chuckle like gravel sliding down a grave. "Shrewd, Commander. You want the fruit without the poison. Very well."

dialogue_steps.speaker: dave
dialogue_steps.text: "Intelligence only. No operational involvement. The League takes Aristotle on its own terms."

dialogue_steps.speaker: death
dialogue_steps.text: A data packet appears on the tactical console. Corsair fleet positions. Crystal cache coordinates. Aristotle's personal contingency plans. "Consider this a free sample," Death whispers. "The next delivery will cost you." The shadow vanishes. Dave stares at the data. It is worth more than a fleet. That is precisely what concerns him.

encounters.title: Knight Emissary
encounters.description: A Knight Order vessel arrives under diplomatic colours, its hull emblazoned with the crossed-swords sigil. The emissary is calm, measured, every word chosen with care. "Commander Dave. The Order has observed the escalating conflict with growing concern. We propose a formal alliance. The Knights will lend their fleet and their legitimacy to the League's campaign. In exchange, we require a seat at the table when the crystal governance is decided."

choices.text: "The League welcomes the Order's partnership. Your terms are fair."

outcome.description: Dave shakes the emissary's hand. It is a firm grip, military to military. The Knights bring honour and heavy cruisers. Dave brings strategy and crystal intelligence. Together, they represent a force that even Aristotle cannot ignore.

choices.text: "Operational support, yes. Political power-sharing is premature."

outcome.description: The emissary's expression cools but does not close. "A limited engagement, then. We will revisit the political question when the dust settles." Dave nods. He has gained ships without surrendering authority. The Knights will remember this caution.

choices.text: "The League fights its own wars. We do not need keepers."

outcome.description: The emissary rises stiffly. "Pride before pragmatism, Commander. A curious choice for a dog of war." The Knight vessel departs. Dave watches it go. He has kept the League's independence. Whether that independence will survive the coming storm is another question.

encounters.title: Coalition Building
encounters.description: Dave spreads the alliance map across his desk. Alien technology. Aristotle's intentions. Death's treachery. Knight honour. Wolf hunger. Lion pride. Every faction a variable in an equation with no clean solution. He pours another glass of water. Drinks it. Sets the glass down with precision. Then he begins to draw lines between the factions. Some will be bridges. Others will be barriers. This is the architecture of the endgame.

choices.text: "Wolves. Knights. Heavy fleet. We end this with overwhelming force."

outcome.description: Dave drafts the coalition charter in military language: chain of command, rules of engagement, victory conditions. The wolves grin. The knights salute. It is a war machine, precise and lethal. Dave does not smile. Machines do not smile. They execute.

choices.text: "A council of all factions. Even the Corsairs. Legitimacy through inclusion."

outcome.description: Dave sends invitations to every faction, including a carefully worded one to Aristotle. The responses trickle in. Some hostile, some cautious, all engaged. Dave has traded military advantage for political ground. It is a gamble. He does not gamble. But this is not gambling. This is diplomacy.

choices.text: "No coalition. The League stands alone. We answer to no one."

outcome.description: Dave burns the alliance map. The League will fight with its own fleet, its own resources, its own doctrine. No wolf demands. No lion egos. No fairy tricks. No knight conditions. Just the mission. Dave sits alone in the war room and plans the final campaign. Alone is familiar. Alone is clean.

encounters.title: Pirate Harassment
encounters.description: Corsair raiders hit a League supply convoy on the outer rim. Fast ships, hit-and-run tactics. The signature style of Aristotle's fleet: arrogant, precise, and infuriating. By the time Dave's reinforcements arrive, the raiders are gone and three supply ships are venting atmosphere.

choices.text: "Double the escorts. Assign interceptor wings to every convoy."

outcome.description: Dave reallocates fleet resources. It stretches the blockade thin but protects the supply lines. A defensive choice. Dave does not prefer defence, but he refuses to lose ships to a cat's ego.

choices.text: "Bait convoy. Skeleton crew, heavy escort hiding in the debris field."

outcome.description: The trap is set with clinical precision. When the Corsair raiders descend on the bait, League warships emerge from the asteroid field like steel jaws closing. The raiders scatter, leaving wreckage and salvage. Dave watches the combat replay once. Then deletes it. The result is what matters.
